purpose: This shows why we needed new kinds of numbers: natural, integers, rational and real. You sort numbers into nested rings, zoom in on the number line, and test which sets are closed under adding and multiplying.

stops.title: The number rings
stops.text: In step 2 the picture shows four rings inside each other: N inside Z inside Q inside R. The numbers to place sit in a tray below. Tap a number, then drag it into the smallest ring that holds it. In other steps the stage is a number line.
stops.try: In step 2, drag 7 into the ring you think holds it, after you answer the prediction.

stops.title: Pick an equation
stops.text: Only in step 1. Each equation has a solution that may not exist in a smaller set. Pick one, then press the smallest set (N, Z, Q or R) that holds the solution, or None yet. The number line changes to that set.
stops.try: Pick x + 3 = 1 style equations and press N. Read why it is not enough.

stops.title: Choose and place
stops.text: Only in step 2. You must answer the prediction first. Then use Previous and Next to choose a number, and press N, Z, Q or R for the innermost set that holds it. You can also drag it on the picture. A wrong choice says why.
stops.try: Try 0 and the square root of 9. Both surprise many students.

stops.title: Also belongs to
stops.text: Only in step 2, after you place a number. Tick every set that contains the chosen number, then check. Because the rings are nested, a number in one ring is also in every ring around it.
stops.try: Place 2/3, then tick Q and R only and check.

stops.title: Zoom in on the line
stops.text: Only in step 3. Each button halves the window on the number line. The readout shows a rational and an irrational number inside the window. However far you zoom, both kinds are still there, and the square root of 2 sits in a gap.
stops.try: Press Half that holds square root of 2 eight times and read the numbers.

stops.title: Does it stay inside?
stops.text: Only in step 4. Each example adds or multiplies two numbers. Decide: is the result rational, irrational, or does it depend? Next example moves on. The picture shows where the result lands on the line.
stops.try: Find an example where two irrational numbers give a rational one.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: There is no menu to switch parts. Each step changes the whole tool: 1 equations, 2 nested rings, 3 zoom, 4 closure. Use Back and Next to move between them.

teacher: Project step 2 and ask the class to predict before anyone drags. Students often think a square root is always irrational, so keep the square root of 9 and 22/7 in view. Use step 3 to ask whether the rationals have gaps even though they are everywhere.
